decision: derive readiness metrics from append-only campaign events

alternatives.name: trust a precomputed campaign summary
alternatives.correctness: weakest; producer bugs can hide duplicate or unresolved operations
alternatives.regressionRisk: high because metric derivation is outside the tested gate

alternatives.name: deterministic JSONL event collector
alternatives.correctness: strong; readiness counters are derived from raw synthetic campaign events
alternatives.robustness: strong; malformed or unknown events fail closed
alternatives.latency: low and linear in event count
alternatives.resourceUse: low; bounded by unique mutation/request keys plus latency samples
alternatives.regressionRisk: low; output matches the existing readiness-gate contract

alternatives.name: central telemetry/database service
alternatives.robustness: strong but adds network and service dependencies
alternatives.regressionRisk: highest for the current lab stage

whyItWon: The JSONL collector independently reconstructs the four correctness gates and latency samples from raw events while preserving the existing readiness evaluator. It adds no network listener or external infrastructure and can consume qrexec-produced logs offline.
failuresAndLessons: A readiness gate is only as trustworthy as its input; accepting counters directly allows instrumentation bugs to mask regressions.
Unknown event types must fail closed so schema drift cannot silently reduce coverage.
Mutation identity must be stable across retries; the campaign harness must emit the same mutationKey for the same logical committed mutation.
safety: synthetic defensive Qubes validation only; no real financial transactions or payment data
